text:
olivia: Hey - customer reported their payment went through but the receipt email was missing line items. They got an 'invoice link' instead.
support-bot: New ticket created: #9241, forwarding logs to @rc and @sanjay :eyes:
rc: Can you paste the original API payload and the service response? Also which model/runtime was used?
olivia: Here's the original function call captured from the app (redacted):
```json
{
  "tool": "send_receipt",
  "args": {
    "order_id": "ord_4Yz",
    "user_email": "user+redacted@example.com"
  }
}
```
But our audit shows the router invoked `email_invoice` instead. The returned payload: 
```json
{
  "invoked_tool": "email_invoice",
  "status": "ok",
  "body": {
    "invoice_url": "https://billing.redwood.example/inv/abc123"
  }
}
```
That explains the missing line items (invoice link is generic).
rc: Hmm. Did the function signatures change recently? We patched email helpers last week.
sanjay: Looking at the router logs, the selector matched on name tokens and favored `email_*` for anything with 'email' or 'invoice' tokens. The model call included a short user intent: "send receipt to user with order details". The selector heuristics are simple n-gram match + schema compatibility — both `send_receipt` and `email_invoice` have compatible schemas (they both accept order_id and email). That allowed the wrong pick.
maya: Customer is upset because they need a line-itemized receipt for expense reports. Can we hotfix routing or map aliases? We should also check whether the model suggested a different tool in the call payload.
rc: Do we have the original model output (the tool call suggested by the assistant)? If the assistant emitted `send_receipt` but router swapped it, that's a bug in the resolver. If assistant emitted `email_invoice`, we need to improve model guidance.
olivia: I captured the assistant/LM payload from the SDK logs. It actually emitted: 
```json
{"name":"send_receipt","args":"{\"order_id\":\"ord_4Yz\",\"email\":\"user+redacted@example.com\"}"}
```
So LM asked for send_receipt.
sanjay: Then the resolver misrouted. We have a rule that prefers the tool with higher literal name overlap when multiple schemas validate. There's a recent change (PR #421) that added lax alias matching — looks like it boosted email_invoice priority.
eng-oncall: Pushing a quick rule revert to canopy branch to disfavor wildcard alias boosts. Will run a canary for 30m. Timeline ~15 min for rollout.
rc: For support remediation, can we trigger send_receipt manually for this order and confirm line items? Also add a customer note apologizing and include receipt attachment.
maya: I've queued a manual send via admin UI. Sending now.
Status: success. Receipt with line items delivered to user. Customer confirmed receipt and will re-open ticket if any issues.
olivia: Thanks. For follow-up: can we add a guard that refuses to switch tools if the assistant explicitly named the tool in the LM output? That would prevent resolver overrides when the assistant decided.
sanjay: Good suggestion. Short-term: revert PR #421 to restore old tie-breaker. Mid-term: implement explicit-honoring flag — if LM emits a tool name verbatim, resolver must prefer it unless schema mismatch. I'll open an RFC and link here.
rc: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/tool-resolver-honor-explicit.md
eng-oncall: Canary deploy completed: reverted alias boost. No regressions for 30m. Rolling to prod now (eta 12m).
maya: Also we should add an alert when resolver chooses a different tool than LM emitted — that would help catch these before they hit customers.
olivia: Agreed. I'll add it to the support runbook: "If customer receipts are missing but payment succeeded, check function invocations -> ensure send_receipt was the invoked tool; if not, escalate to eng-oncall."
rc: Closing ticket for now since manual send succeeded and canary appears healthy. Reopen if the customer reports further issues.
support-bot: Ticket #9241 closed by rc. :white_check_mark:
